To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

coastal users have different values and interests, and that geovisualisations that can capture and reflect these different values and interests have potential for supporting collaboration and coastal management.
coastal geovisuality research needs to focus on how coastal user groups relate to and understand their coastal environments as places and not just as spaces.

(i) geovisuals can be used to support collaboration between conflicting coastal user groups; (ii) the design of geovisual tools for coastal management should consider the cultural values and understandings of coastal places held by user groups; and (iii) geovisuality can support coastal management by providing tools that enable the visualization of place-based information and the development of place-based solutions to coastal management issues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how geovisualisations can be used to facilitate collaboration among conflicting coastal users by capturing the range of values, meanings and behaviours that are associated with coastal places.
developing geovisualisations that can be used to support collaborative coastal planning and management by reflecting the range of values associated with coastal places.
developing geovisual tools that are able to capture the place-based values of a range of coastal user groups and to facilitate collaborative coastal management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
geovisualisation is the process and product of visualisation of geospatial data and information.
the geovisualisation of coastal places can be used to help facilitate collaboration and consensus among conflicting user groups.
geovisualisations that are immersive and realistic are most effective at conveying place-based information and can be used as tools for collaborative coastal planning and management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
geovisualisations can be a useful tool for supporting collaboration among coastal user groups, but they need to reflect the place-based values and meanings associated with coastal environments.
coastal geovisulations can support collaborative coastal management by facilitating the integration of different user groups’ values and meanings into the planning process.

coastal geovisuality research can benefit from a focus on the place-based values, meanings and understandings of different user groups, and that this research can provide a foundation for developing geovisual tools that are better able to facilitate collaborative coastal management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
geovisuals should be developed with the goal of supporting collaboration between coastal user groups, and not as an end in themselves.

coastal geovisuality research needs to move beyond simply creating geovisual tools for communicating coastal information, toward developing geovisualities that facilitate collaboration among user groups.

the design of coastal geovisulations should be informed by an understanding of how coastal user groups relate to their coastal environments, and how these relationships can be reflected in geovisualisations.
